This is what the server SENDS to clients after category voting resolves. It is NOT authored by hand — the server picks N question IDs from quiz-mode-question-bank.json for the winning category, then fills in each lock's config below. Schema matches existing scenarios/*/puzzles.json conventions (id/type/ui/config/mandatory).

UPDATED to reflect the 7-category bank (aws-core-services, agentic-ai, security, vietnam-aws, startups-innovation, cloud-fundamentals, FrugalArchitect), 81 core entries each for the first 6 (plus a per-category spelling set); FrugalArchitect was curated down to 82 = 622 total. This example uses 'agentic-ai' as the winning category to demonstrate the current, event-relevant content (Kiro CLI 3.0, Amazon Quick, AgentCore).
_note_keypad_word: keypad-lock and word-lock take ONE question each. Server picks 1 numeric-type question for keypad, 1 word-type question for word-lock. No internal pool/shuffle exists in these components — the server's per-session pick IS the randomization.

falseOutputs: Access denied. That vault belongs to a different era.

config._note: CORRECTED from earlier draft: the backend, NOT the client, must resolve each '{correctValue|wrongValue}' slot before sending anything over the wire (see quiz-mode-handoff.md, Backend section 3). Sending the raw two-sided template to the client would let a player inspect network traffic and see both values before answering. This example shows the ALREADY-RESOLVED payload the client receives — the raw templates are shown only for reference, they are NOT part of the actual wire payload.

statements.text: Kiro CLI 3.0 is built on a unified agent harness shared with Kiro IDE and Kiro Web.
Kiro CLI 3.0 fully supports Amazon Linux 2 (AL2), requiring CLI 2.x there instead.
Amazon Bedrock AgentCore reached general availability in October 2025.
The Amazon Nova 2 family, announced at re:Invent December 2025, has two models.

config._note: spelling-lock takes a pool of answer words/phrases and randomly draws `pickCount` of them per instance, presenting each as its own shuffled-letter anagram (no unrelated decoy letters — every letter shown belongs in the answer). No internal reshuffle-on-loop since it's a fixed pick, not an infinite pool cycle. onSubmit() fires with no arguments once all pickCount words are solved in sequence; onWrong(msg) fires per wrong spelling attempt and should be wired to the engine's onFail penalty helper, same as keypad/word/pillar. Multi-word answers (e.g. 'Kiro Power' below) ARE supported — spelling-lock renders a visible gap in the slot layout at each space, so word boundaries stay visible even though the letter pool itself has spaces stripped. Pull from the bank's dedicated `spelling` array (NOT `word`) — every entry there is pre-filtered to letters+spaces only, 5-16 letters excluding spaces.

wager-lock also shuffles order + reshuffles internally, and randomizes which decoys are visible per stake tier. Server only supplies the pool. Stakes array below uses the SINGLE-ENTRY form (see quiz-mode-instructions-engine.md 'Wager-lock stake default' section) — this auto-skips the Safe/Confident/All-In picker and always shows 4 choices.
